newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee says it welcomes NRC scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee says it welcomes NRC scrutiny.

text.p: Maine Yankee said Wednesday it sees the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) decision to add its plant to its watchlist of nuclear plants as an opportunity to rebuild public confidence in the plant.

"Maine Yankee has taken steps in recent months to aggressively address concerns raised by the NRC and we are significantly ahead of schedule in our efforts to implement an array of improvements at Maine Yankee," said Graham Leitch, vice president of operations for the plant.
Maine Yankee said it is spending $30 million to improve its plant, including upgrades and hiring additional staff, primarily in maintenance and engineering.
The 910 megawatt nuclear plant, in Wiscasset, Maine, was placed on the NRC's watchlist Wednesday as a category two plant, which permits Maine Yankee to operate while improvements continue.
Maine Yankee is one of eight nuclear powr facilities currently on the NRC's watchlist, which means it requires regulatory oversight because of declining performance.
The plant has been off line since December 6 to sort out problems with the plant's cabling. Maine Yankee said it expects to complete work in mid-March.

Maine Yankee is operated by Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co, a consortium made up of Central Maine Power Co (38 percent), New England Electric System (20), Northeast Utilities (20), Bangor Hydro (7), Maine Public Service Co (5), and 10 percent by other regional utilities.
